objects.title: A strong polyhedral domain for a positive semidefinite translation pencil
objects.model: A rational exact sequence 0→U→L→R→0, a countable faithful rational action G preserving a full-dimensional convex cone ℂ⊂L and the exact-sequence subspace, and its image on R.
objects.statement: If the base image has a strong rational polyhedral domain B, the actual real fibres over B are s(d)+im T_d for a rational section s and normalized rational self-adjoint positive semidefinite pencil T, and a full translation lattice is normal of finite index in the base kernel, then ℂ has one rational polyhedral domain with full closed-translate separation and trivial setwise stabilizer.
objects.quantifiers: Every such rational sequence, group and cone; every real d in every face of B; the full group G, including nonsplit finite extensions of its translations.
assumptions: B covers the base cone and satisfies Li–Zhao Definition 3.4 for the faithful base image.

In a rational positive definite scalar product the operators T_d for d in B are self-adjoint positive semidefinite, a positive combination of the rational generator operators is positive definite, and T_H=I at some rational H.
The entire fibre equals s(d)+im T_d at each real d in B. The full lattice acts by x↦x+T_{πx}z and is normal of finite index in the base kernel.
objects.scope: A theorem with explicit hypotheses on a group action and an effective fibre description; rational lineality of auxiliary cones is allowed.
objects.objections: Without the exact boundary fibres or the finite-index lattice assumption, this result makes no assertion about a particular geometric action.
sources: Rational polyhedral Dirichlet construction of informed-a and Main, RUN rmkc-boss1-20261123-a1.
Li–Zhao, Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. 131 (2025), e70099, Definition 3.4; the exact whole-translate condition is used.

objects.title: Finite kernel modulo vertical divisors and lifting a domain on the actual cone
objects.model: A complex klt Calabi–Yau fibration with normal projective Q-factorial total space and normal quasi-projective base; existence of good minimal models for effective klt pairs in its relative dimension. Γ is the relative numerical pseudoautomorphism group preserving the boundary support (or its coefficients).
objects.statement: Let T be the span of all vertical prime divisor classes and p:V→V/T. Then the action on T and the kernel of the action on V/T are finite. For rational relatively ample a its stabilizer over p(a) is finite. Any full-dimensional weak rational polyhedral domain on p(C) with finite stabilizer lifts and refines to a strong rational polyhedral domain on the actual C for all of Γ.
objects.quantifiers: Every such fibration, every rational relatively ample a, and every qualifying weak quotient domain; no assumption that all directions of the closed movable cone are effective.
assumptions: The relative numerical group uses all complete curves contracted by f.
For the lifting conclusion, the image in GL(V/T) acts on the actual p(C) with the stated quotient domain.
Low relative dimension at most two verifies the good-model premise used for the target.
objects.scope: Vertical classes of both signs are relatively effective. This controls the kernel on V/T and transfers full closed-translate separation; the base need not be Q-factorial.
objects.objections: The kernel on V/T is distinct from the kernel after division by all lineality of the closed movable cone; the latter need not be finite.
sources: Informed-a and Main, RUN rmkc-boss1-20261123-a1, finite vertical kernel and domain lifting.

Hacon–Xu, arXiv:1107.4149v2, Corollary 1.6, and Z. Li, arXiv:2006.01370v1, Definition 3.1, Remark 3.2 and Corollary 1.2; the integral round-down proof applies to every effective real perturbation of the same-support rational klt working pair.

objects.title: Generic Picard realization of the effective movable cone and its actual group
objects.model: For every complex terminal Calabi–Yau fibre space f:(X,Δ)→S in the Li–Zhao sense, with X normal, projective and Q-factorial, K_X+Δ numerically trivial over S, and dim X−dim S in {0,1,2}. Include all admissible effective real boundaries, arbitrary absolute dimension and arbitrary allowed base. Use the full faithful numerical image Γ of the relative support-preserving pseudo-automorphisms on V=N¹(X/S)_R, defined by all complete contracted curves. The cone is C=closure(Mov(X/S))∩Eff(X/S).
objects.statement: For positive relative dimension and absolute dimension at least two, quotient by the span of vertical primes identifies L_Q with Pic(F)_Q/J with J⊂Pic⁰(F)(k)_Q. The image p(C) is the image of the actual effective generically nef Picard classes. Its generic numerical image D has a strong rational polyhedral domain B for the actual relative-group image. If U=Pic⁰(F)(k)_R/J_R is nonzero, all real fibres above B, the pencil T, the invariant scalar product and the finite-index full translation lattice verify the operator theorem's hypotheses. For U=0 the projected cone identifies with D. The zero-dimensional relative and low absolute cases satisfy the elementary alternatives stated in the body.
objects.quantifiers: Every fibration in the geometric hypotheses; all real points of all faces of B, all components of the admissible boundary, and the whole actual relative numerical group including its finite holonomy.
assumptions: The original target hypotheses only; the generic field is k=C(S).
In the positive-dimensional realization the projection T is by vertical prime classes in the numerical space defined by all contracted curves.
objects.scope: Covers the actual Picard, effective and numerical images and the full group in the original problem. It includes the cases U=0, q=1, and q=2 and the elementary boundary cases.
objects.objections: The covering on generic numerical classes descends from the geometric surface using a finite Albanese marking and Galois-fixed actual automorphisms. Extension of a finite-index subgroup suffices at the subsequent projection from the relative group. Both assertions concern their specified faithful numerical images.

body.section: Realization on the generic Picard group

objects.title: Strong relative Morrison–Kawamata movable cone theorem in relative dimension at most two
objects.model: For every complex terminal Calabi–Yau fibre space f:(X,Δ)→S in the Li–Zhao sense, with X normal, projective and Q-factorial, K_X+Δ numerically trivial over S, and dim X−dim S in {0,1,2}. Include all admissible effective real boundaries, arbitrary absolute dimension and arbitrary allowed base. Use the full faithful numerical image Γ of the relative support-preserving pseudo-automorphisms on V=N¹(X/S)_R, defined by all complete contracted curves. The cone is C=closure(Mov(X/S))∩Eff(X/S).
objects.statement: There is one rational polyhedral cone Π⊂C such that ΓΠ=C, γΠ∩Int Π is empty for every nonidentity γ∈Γ, and Stab_Γ(Π) is trivial, exactly as in Li–Zhao Definition 3.4.
objects.quantifiers: Every terminal pair over C satisfying the full stipulated fibre-space definition, for relative dimensions zero, one and two; no bound on dim X, base Q-factoriality, restriction on fibre type, or nondegeneracy assumption.
assumptions: Exactly the geometric data in the model; relative numerical equivalence is as in Li–Zhao. All boundary coefficients admitted by the terminal pair convention are included.
objects.scope: The whole original quantified strong statement, including effective boundary faces, degeneracy of the closed movable cone and full closed-translate separation.
objects.objections: The open original problem registration preserves its input bytes and version. This separate theorem supplies a full-scope mathematical answer through the directed implication to that registration.
sources: Complete proof V3 by the informed lines, the contributor of the marked generic descent, and Main, RUN rmkc-boss1-20261123-a1; §7 and its accompanying audit identify the primary sources and prove the required scope.
